items.title: AWS Lambda now supports orchestrating MicroVMs with Lambda durable functions
items.content_snippet: Today, AWS announces a developer preview of a new extension for orchestrating Lambda MicroVMs with Lambda durable functions . The extension adds durable operations for running work on MicroVMs and managing their lifecycle. You can use the new operations to build software factories, security scanners, or orchestrate CI/CD jobs that run untrusted or agent-generated code in isolated sandboxes. items.title: Amazon CloudWatch Omni now integrates with PagerDuty
items.content_snippet: Amazon CloudWatch Omni alerts can now automatically create PagerDuty incidents, so notifications flow directly into your existing incident management workflows. This reduces mean time to resolution (MTTR) by eliminating manual notification steps and ensuring consistent incident workflows. CloudWatch Omni is a fully managed AI-powered observability experience built on open standards that unifies monitoring for AI agents, applications, and infrastructure. items.title: Stop Building Software Factories — Justin McCarthy, Diffusion
items.content_snippet: Most of the time you don't know what you want yet, so putting new ideas through a factory wastes time and tokens. Justin McCarthy, founder and CEO of Diffusion, argues for brownfield factories instead: continuous loops that keep the promises of software customers already pay for, getting faster, cheaper and safer around the clock. items.title: 1,000 Claude Agents Formalized Fermat's Last Theorem — Lance Martin, Anthropic
items.content_snippet: A team of 1,000 Claude agents formalized Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean over about 30 hours, using nothing but Git and a database, with no domain-specific harness and no human steering on the solution. Lance Martin shows how the lead agent built its own coordination tables and how the team reassigned itself as the work progressed.
